statement: CoreWeave and NVIDIA claim the Vera Rubin NVL72 delivers one-tenth the cost per million tokens versus Blackwell.
why: A large drop in the cost of serving tokens makes inference-heavy products cheaper to run, which historically expands usage volumes faster than unit prices fall.

impact.mechanism: Cheaper serving economics lower the price floor for inference, encouraging more token volume and therefore more accelerator hours consumed overall.

evidence.excerpt: one-tenth the cost per million tokens

confidence.basis: Unverified vendor economics claim with no workload definition or pricing detail, from one secondary source.
